head.title: ProjectForge 9.0: a new frontend, Wicket retired, all libraries up to date
intro: ProjectForge 9.0 is a major update. The classic Wicket user interface was replaced by **projectforge-next**, a new frontend built with Next.js and React, and all libraries were brought up to date. It also brings a problem dashboard for operations, many new charts with key figures, robust interfaces to external systems, e-invoicing and an identity provider integration. The development builds leading up to it are listed in the changelog as 8.2 snapshots.

overview: **New frontend projectforge-next:** all pages migrated, including calendar, time sheets, order book, invoices, structure tree, access rights, monthly report, liquidity planning and administration. The classic Wicket module has been removed.

**Problem dashboard:** log events are classified and aggregated into problems with a persistent status, with links into the log viewer, a JSON export for an AI-assisted analysis and prioritized error digest mails instead of one mail per error.

**Charts and key figures:** order statistics with budget scenario, contribution margins, forecast, invoicing and net sum charts with a year-earlier comparison, invoicing quota and error figures in the system statistics.

**Robust interfaces:** timeouts, connection pools, bounded sync threads and sync statistics for LDAP, identity provider, iCal, SMS, Sipgate and the gateway; an unreachable system fails fast instead of blocking, failing calendar subscriptions are retried with a growing interval.
**E-invoicing:** XRechnung and ZUGFeRD export of outgoing invoices, PEPPOL validation, cancellation invoices and an e-invoice checker.
**Identity provider:** synchronization of users, groups and passwords with Authentik or Keycloak (module projectforge-idp).
**Finance:** recurring liquidity entries, DATEV import of incoming invoices, salary import, currency conversion with online exchange rates.
**Technology:** Spring Boot 4.1, Spring 7, Hibernate 7.4, Hibernate Search 8.4, Tomcat 11, Kotlin 2.3, Next.js 16, React 19, TanStack Table.

items.title: projectforge-next
items: New frontend built with Next.js and React, with light and dark theme, compact top navigation and a quick access search for the menu.
Tables with column filters, pinning, reordering, saved layouts and filter favorites; multi selection and mass update for many entities.
Login with two-factor authentication and password reset under `/next/login`; *stay logged in* with one token per device.

items.title: E-invoicing
items: XRechnung export and ZUGFeRD PDF with embedded XML, PEPPOL validation, invoice attachments embedded in the export.

Identity provider integration (module projectforge-idp): users, groups and passwords synchronized with Authentik or Keycloak, including WLAN password hashes.

items.title: Problem dashboard
items: Log events are classified at the call site and aggregated in the database into problems with a persistent status.
Dashboard with tiles per subsystem, links into the log viewer, search of a problem's occurrences in the log files and an export as JSON for an AI-assisted analysis.
Prioritized error digest mails per audience instead of one mail per error; early digest for new security and data problems.

items.title: Charts and key figures
items: Order statistics with its own filter, charts, data tables, budget scenario and warnings about lost budgets.
Contribution margins in the order book, forecast charts, net sum charts of outgoing invoices and invoice statistics with a year-earlier comparison.
Invoicing quota as a chart and in *My statistics*; error figures in the system statistics.
Recurring series in the liquidity planning.
Address import and export as vCard and from free text, with a diff view and a warning about duplicates.
Incoming invoices imported from DATEV, with currency and exchange rates looked up online.
Gateway for external data transfer with delta sync, CardDAV favorites and a public heartbeat.
ICS import of team events with a diff preview.
Changelog with news, search and highlighting under `/next/changelog`, also in German.

All pages migrated to projectforge-next, among them calendar, time sheets, order book, outgoing and incoming invoices, structure tree, access rights, monthly report, liquidity planning, DATEV and salary import, HR planning, Gantt charts and administration; links and bookmarks of the classic pages lead to the new ones.
Configurable customer groups and business units as filters for time sheets, invoices, projects and orders.
Structure element picker with recently used entries and favorites; JIRA issue links in lists and forms.
Server-side paging of order and invoice lists; deleted entries can be restored.

items.title: Robust interfaces
items: Timeouts and shared connection pools for LDAP, identity provider, iCal, SMS, Sipgate and the gateway, configurable per interface.
An unreachable or too slow system fails fast with one warning instead of blocking; sync runs use bounded threads instead of a new thread per trigger.
Failing calendar subscriptions are retried with a growing interval and deactivated after 90 days.
Sync statistics with timing and counts per run, shown in the system statistics.
Order book and invoices no longer freeze when two caches refresh at once.
Many N+1 query floods removed; large ID lists stay under the database's bind parameter limit.
Subscribed calendars, the MS Project export of Gantt charts, the Word-to-PDF conversion and the LDAP sync repaired.
CSRF protection and complete field validation for the REST calls; access checks for all REST endpoints, enforced by an architecture test.
Security review of the filter chain: trusted proxies, client IP detection, throttling, safe redirect URLs.
2FA required for sensitive pages; deleted groups never grant access rights.
Module projectforge-wicket with all classic pages, Wicket-only i18n keys and libraries no longer used.
AG Grid (replaced by TanStack Table), react-scripts (replaced by Vite) and JAXB.
Legacy XML user preferences are migrated to the JSON store.
Spring Boot 4.1, Spring 7, Hibernate 7.4, Hibernate Search 8.4, Tomcat 11.
Kotlin 2.3, JUnit 6, Gradle 9.8, Next.js 16, React 19, TanStack Table, Vite and Vitest.
Versions are numbered X.Y.Z and built by a release script, the version is set in one place.

updates.title: ProjectForge 9.0.16 released
summary: **Chat**: rooms, direct messages, files, threads, mentions and confidential messages
**Search** ignores accents and umlaut spellings

overview: **Chat** (menu Common → Chat): rooms with chosen users and groups, and direct messages to any user, readable by their participants only, administrators neither. Messages with formatting, files of any type (stored in the data transfer), emoji reactions, threads that can be followed and marked unread, and @ mentions notified in the app and by mail. Confidential messages in direct messages are end-to-end encrypted and never stored by the server. Behind a reverse proxy, the chat needs an unbuffered connection, see the administration guide.

**Search:** search and selection boxes ignore accents and German umlaut spellings ("Mueller" finds "Müller", "Strasse" finds "Straße"), completely after the next nightly re-index; deactivated users are no longer found in the search of the main menu.
**Administration:** the backup script of the administration guide compresses the dump of the files to about half the size.

**Fixed:** the order and invoice caches refreshed each other endlessly when an invoice referred to a deleted order position; projects are found by their number and the name of their customer; outgoing invoices saved in the new interface are found by their customer at once; the time sheet filter for sub structure elements can be switched off; postal codes like "D-34286" are no longer linked as JIRA issues; the log of a running script is shown again.

items: Chat: confidential messages in direct messages (e.g. for a password), end-to-end encrypted in both browsers, relayed live and never stored by the server, shown to the recipient only once.

items.title: Chat
items: Chat rooms (menu Common → Chat): anybody creates a room and chooses its participants, users and groups; members who join a group later take part at once. The creator and the moderators edit and delete the room. Rooms are visible to their participants only, administrators included.

Direct messages: anybody can write privately to any user shown in the user selection, from the chat page, from a user found in the menu search (start chat / send file; for everybody, with the users of the user selection) or by clicking an author in any conversation; whoever got a message can answer. Only the two read the conversation, administrators neither.

Messages with formatting (text colours, lists, links, inline code and code blocks of several lines), files of any type (paste, drag & drop or file dialog; images as thumbnails), emoji reactions and replies as threads of their own, which can be followed. The files are stored in the data transfer: in an area per room, whose participants see it in the data transfer and where the files are kept as long as chosen in the room; files of direct messages go into the personal box of the recipient. Without the data transfer plugin, no files are exchanged. Own messages can be edited and deleted, moderators hide messages with a reason and see the history of a message.

Typing @ suggests the participants of the room; a mentioned person is notified at once, in the app and by mail. New messages are notified once per room until read, by mail only if not seen in the app within an hour; rooms can be muted.
New messages appear without reload (server-sent events, with polling as fallback). Behind a reverse proxy, the chat needs an unbuffered connection, see the administration guide.
Chat: a file of a message can also be opened in its data transfer area, besides downloading it.
Chat: a message can be marked unread, threads with unread replies are marked, and in a thread a line shows the first unread reply.

Search and selection boxes ignore accents and German umlaut spellings: "Andre" finds "André", "Mueller" and "Muller" find "Müller", "Strasse" finds "Straße", and vice versa. Applies to entries indexed after the update, i.e. completely after the next nightly re-index.
Admin guide: the backup script compresses the dump of the files (about half the size), because pg_dump writes their contents hex encoded.
Outgoing invoices: invoices saved in the new interface were not found by the name of their customer until the next search index rebuild.
JIRA links: an issue key needs at least two leading uppercase letters, so a postal code like "D-34286" in a text is no longer linked as an issue.
Project selection: projects are also found by their number (e.g. 7.002) and by the name of their customer.
Scripts: showing the log of a running script could fail with an error.
Time sheet list: the filter including all sub structure elements could not be switched off. It is replaced by the filter "without structure sub elements", off by default.
The order and invoice caches no longer refresh each other endlessly (e.g. during the daily order book snapshots) when an invoice refers to a deleted order position.
Search in the main menu: deactivated users are no longer found (they still are in the user list).

overview: **Ad hoc bookings:** who may edit the time sheets of others on a structure element grants colleagues the booking of own time sheets for a period, optionally restricted to some cost units; the colleagues see only the granted structure elements. Employees without this right may propose such a booking, the project management accepts the time sheets afterwards (reminded by a new notification rule).

**Notifications:** delivery steps by SMS; new rule "Creditor invoices due"; the rule editor lists the variables for subject and text with example values and a copy button, the preview shows the texts with example values.
**Creditor invoices:** marked as overdue already 2 working days before the due date.

**Customer wizard:** existing structure elements of the customer and the project can be used instead of new ones, picked from the tree or found by the same title.
**Order statistics:** the bubble size of the contribution margin chart shows the contribution margin; titles can be switched on.

**Fixed:** structure elements created or moved during a background reload could vanish from the structure tree, the responsible person was missing after a change; an invalid search syntax shows a hint instead of an empty list; the info of a structure element is only answered to users who may see it; the password reset mail is limited per user, per client and in total, so it can no longer be requested over and over.

items.title: Ad hoc bookings
items: Who may edit the time sheets of others on a structure element (e.g. project management, finance) may grant colleagues the booking of own time sheets for a period, without group membership: several colleagues at once, on the structure element and any of its sub elements, each optionally restricted to some of its cost units. The grant is active right away, each colleague gets a mail with the links to book on.

The colleagues see only the granted structure elements and the titles of their ancestors in the structure tree: no other structure elements, consumption, time sheets of others or statistics. After the period or a revocation the own time sheets stay readable.
In the structure tree, a badge marks the structure elements with ad hoc bookings; its tooltip names the colleagues and their periods. Shown only to who may grant on the structure element.

Employees without this right may propose such a booking on the structure elements they book on themselves, for 31 days at most: the colleague books right away, the project management accepts the time sheets afterwards, unchanged or moved to another structure element or cost unit (time sheet form or mass update; list filter "Only to be accepted"). Until then they count like any other time sheet. The project management may confirm a proposal, so later bookings don't have to be accepted anymore.

New notification rule "Time sheets to be accepted": reminds the project managers of the time sheets still to be accepted (in the app, and by mail if not acknowledged, as configured in the rule). The structure tree shows their number next to the badge.
Consumption bar (structure tree, task list, time sheet form): the tooltip shows the budget, the booked and the remaining person days as a calculation, an overbooked budget in red.
Time sheet form: the recently used entries show the consumption of their budget, and the search also matches it.

items.title: Creditor invoices
items: Marked as overdue (red) already 2 working days before the due date, so they are paid in time.

New notification rule "Creditor invoices due": reports unpaid creditor invoices due within a configurable number of working days (overdue ones of the last 90 days included) to the recipients of the rule.

items.title: Notifications
items: The rule editor lists the variables available for subject and text (general ones and those of the rule type), each with a button to copy it.
The variables come with an example value each, so it is visible how e.g. a list of invoices looks; the preview also shows the texts with example values.
Time sheet form: the table of recently used entries can be sorted and filtered per column, its columns can be reordered, resized, pinned and hidden; the layout is remembered per user.
Notifications: delivery steps by SMS to the mobile phone number of the recipients (if SMS is configured), with an own SMS text of the rule or otherwise the subject and the link.

Customer wizard: existing structure elements of the customer and the project can be used instead of new ones, picked from the tree (the title may differ, e.g. "ACME" for "ACME Inc.") or found automatically by the same title.

Order statistics, contribution margin bubble chart: the size of a bubble shows its contribution margin instead of its costs. The switch "Show titles" labels the own bubbles with their short title and contribution margin %; switched off, the names are in the tooltip only.
The info of a structure element (title, path, project, customer, consumption) was answered to every logged-in user; now only to users who may see the structure element.

Structure tree: a structure element created or moved while the tree was being reloaded in the background could vanish from the tree until the next reload, so no sub-element could be created below it ("Parent structure element is required but not found").
Structure tree: after a structure element was changed, its responsible person was missing in the tree until the next reload.
Password forgotten: the reset mail is limited per user, per client and in total, so it can no longer be requested over and over (mail bombing, invalidating a pending reset link).
Lists: a search term that isn't a valid search syntax (e.g. "Project: Alpha") now shows a hint instead of an empty list without explanation.

items: Order statistics, contribution margin: bubble chart of revenue, contribution margin % and costs (size) per project, project group, customer or customer group. On request, the other projects of the selection (e.g. of the whole business unit) are shown for comparison, anonymously. The bubbles take the colors of the business units, set with the business units (customer groups page).
